questions.prompt: You start a session in ~/notes, then `git init` a repo at ~/projects/api and `cd` into it in your own terminal. The agent still edits files under ~/notes. Why?
options: Git caches the folder a session began in, and only updates after you commit
The agent's working directory was set when the session started and does not follow your terminal
The agent cannot edit files outside the folder it was launched from
`cd` in your terminal is scoped to your terminal, so the agent sees a different prompt
questions.explanation: The working directory is decided once, at session start, and does not move as you talk to the agent. Fix: say the folder explicitly at the start of a session, or restart the session in the repo. Option C sounds right but is wrong — the agent can reach any folder you grant; it simply defaults to the session's folder.

questions.prompt: You are deep in a repo at repo/src/components/Button/. Which single command reliably tells you the folder you should report problems against?
questions.explanation: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` prints the repo root regardless of how deep you are. `pwd` is right when you want your current subfolder and wrong when you want the project — and it will disagree with the path in a stack trace.

questions.prompt: A colleague's `git commit` fails with an error mentioning identity. Nothing in the repo looks wrong. What is the actual cause?
options: The repo has no commits yet, so there is nothing to attach a commit to
The branch has diverged from main
`user.name` and `user.email` were never configured on that machine
A file is staged but has never been committed
questions.explanation: Git refuses to attribute a commit to nobody. The other three are real situations but produce different messages — none of them mention identity.
